subject: Circle inscribed in an equilateral triangle

references.reason: Closest bundled relationship: circle, straight boundaries, radii, and tangency. Borrowed hierarchy and restrained geometry, not historical background fills.
references.inspection: Source read and rendered on a light surface via html_preview.

decisions: Triangle and incircle share the primary 0.95-unit stroke. Radii, perpendicular markers, and equality ticks use the standard 0.65-unit stroke at 0.50 opacity.

Solid point markers are explicitly declared geometric-point symbols. T₁, T₂, T₃ identify tangencies; O identifies the center. Three right-angle markers and the equal-radius equation explain the relationship.
Matching side ticks identify the equilateral triangle. No physical dimension or standards-compliance claim is made.
No grid, hatch, or area fill: the three radii already explain the entire construction. Enclosed forms and canvas remain transparent.
Cal Sans, Arial, sans-serif fallback stack; automatic optical sizing, no letter-spacing, no synthesized styles, GEOM 25 for the single text role. No font files required.
Accessible title and description included. No external resources or scripts.

equations: tangent points are the midpoints of the three sides

checks.geometry_source: Actual serialized SVG coordinates recovered with Python XML parser.

visual.result: The circle-in-triangle gesture remains clear at both sizes. At intended size, labels, radius lines, right-angle markers, and equality ticks are separated and visible; thumbnail preserves the form and contact relationship, while the equation is secondary small text.

limitations: Font fallback is allowed and no Cal Sans file was supplied; the exact browser-resolved font was not measured.
This is a standalone light-surface geometric illustration, not a responsive host integration or a physical engineering drawing.
